Disclosure  to  Promote  the  Right  To  Information 

Whereas  the  Parliament  of  India  has  set  out  to  provide  a  practical  regime  of  right  to 
information  for  citizens  to  secure  access  to  information  under  the  control  of  public  authorities, 
in  order  to  promote  transparency  and  accountability  in  the  working  of  every  public  authority, 
and  whereas  the  attached  publication  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  is  of  particular  interest 
to  the  public,  particularly  disadvantaged  communities  and  those  engaged  in  the  pursuit  of 
education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public. 


Mazdoor  Kisan  Shakti  Sangathan 
"The  Right  to  Information,  The  Right  to  Live"

IS:  4569  (  Part  I  )-  1985 


Indian  Standard 
SPECIFICATION  FOR  SCISSORS,  EYE 

PART  1     CORNEAL 
(  Second  Revision  ) 


(  Reaffirmed  2002 ) 


1.  Scope  —  Covers  requirements  for  corneal  scissors  used  in  eye  surgery. 

2.  Shape  and  Dimensions  —  As  shown  in  Fig.  1 ,  2  and  3. 

2.1  Screw  —  Shall  be  of  slotted  cheese  head.  Profile  of  the  screw  thread  shall  conform  to 
IS  :  4218  (  Part  1  )-1976  'Specification  for  basic  and  design  profiles  (first  revision )'. 

2.2  The  tolerance  for  blades  dimensions  shall  conform  to  'fine'  class  of  deviation  and  the  tolerances 
for  other  dimensions  shall  conform  to  'medium'  class  of  deviation  of  IS:  2102  (  Parti  )-1980 
'General  tolerances  for  dimensions  and  form  and  position  :  Part  1  General  tolerances  for  linear  and 
angular  dimensions  (second  revision  )'.

FIG,  2    SCISSORS,  CORNEAL,  ANGLED  ON

2.3  The  joint  shall  be  of  screw-recessed  type  conforming  to  IS  :  3642-1976  'General  requirements  for 
surgical  instruments. 

3.  Material —  Scissors  shall  be  made  of  stainless  steel  conforming  to  Designation  40Cr13  of 
IS  :  6603-1972  'Specification  for  stainless  steel  bars  and  flats'. 

3.1  Screws  shall  be  made  of  the  same  material  as  used  for  scissors. 

4.  Workmanship  and  Finish  —  Scissors  shall  be  free  from  cracks,  seams,  burrs,  pits  and  other 
defects.  Scissors  shall  be  symmetrical  and  well  balanced.  The  blades  shall  close  fully  and  freely 
with  a  continuous  pinch,  without  stuffings  and  excessive  cross-over  action.  There  shall  be  no 
stiffness  play  at  the  joint.  The  edges  shall  be  even  and  rounded  except  for  the  cutting  edge  which 
shall  be  sharp.  The  cutting  edge  shall  not  have  any  feather  and  nick.  The  scissors  shall  be  polished 
bright  and  passivated. 

5.  Hardness  —  550  to  600  HV. 

6.  Tests 

6.1  Performance  —  The  whole  length  of  the  cutting  edges  including  the  tips  shall  cut  wet  tissue  paper, 
teased  out  cotton  wool,  fine  hair  and  frayed  lint  accurately  and  cleanly,  when  worked  with  either  right 
or  left  hand. 

6.2  Corrosion  Resistance  —  The  instrument  shall  satisfy  the  boiling  and  autoclaving  test  as  specified 
in  IS  :  7531  -1 975  'Method  for  boiling  and  autoclaving  test  for  corrosion  resistance  of  stainless  steel 
surgical  instruments'. 

7.  Sampling  and  Criteria  for  Conformity 

7,1  A  suitable  sampling  scheme  and  criteria  for  acceptance  is  given  in  Appendix  A.

CASTROVIEJO'S  PATTERN 


8.  Marking  —  Each  scissors  shall  be  legibly  and  indelibly  marked  with  the  manufacturer's  name, 
initials  or  recognized  trade-mark  and,  in  addition,  the  words  stainless  steel  or  letters  'SS'. 

8.1  IS/  Certification  Marking—  Details  available  with  the  Indian  Standards  Institution. 

9.  Packing  —  Shall  be  packed  as  agreed  to  between  the  purchaser  and  the  supplier.    The  working 
end  shall  be  suitably  protected. 


APPENDIX    A 

(  Clause  7.1  ) 

SAMPLING  AND  CRITERIA  FOR  CONFORMITY  FOR  SCISSORS 


A-1.  Lot  — In  any  consignment,  all  the  scissors  produced  from  the  same  material  under  similar 
conditions  shall  constitute  a  lot. 


IS:  4569  (Part  I)-  1985 

A-2.  The  number  of  scissors  to  be  selected  from  each  lot  shall  depend  upon  the  size  of  the  lot  and 
shall  be  in  accordance  with  the  following  table: 

TABLE  1  SCALE  OF  SAMPLING 

Lot  Size  Sample  Size 

(1)  (2) 

Up  to    15  2 

16     „     50  3 

51     „  150  5 

151  and  above  8 

A-2.1  These  scissors  shall  be  selected  from  the  lot  at  random  and  in  order  to  ensure  the  randomness 
of  selection,  procedures  given  in  IS  :  4905-1968  'Methods  for  random  sampling'  may  be  followed. 

A-3*  Number  of  Tests  and  Criteria  for  Conformity  —  All  the  scissors  selected  at  random  in 
accordance  with  the  table  shall  be  tested  for  shape  and  dimensions,  workmanship  and  finish,  hardness, 
performance  tests  and  corrosion  resistance.  A  scissors  shall  be  considered  as  defective  if  it  fails  to 
meet  any  one  or  more  of  these  requirements  A  lot  shaii  be  considered  as  conforming  to  these 
requirements  if  none  of  the  scissors  in  the  sample  is  found  to  be  defective  in  any  of  these  tests. 


EXPLANATORY    NOTE 

This  standard  was  prepared  in  1968  and  revised  in  1976.  The  present  revision  has  been  taken 
up  to  include  certain  modification  in  order  to  bring  the  specification  in  line  with  the  modern  manufac- 
turing practices.  The  non-functional  dimensions  have  been  rounded  off.  The  tolerance  for  the 
functional  dimensions  have  been  modified  keeping  in  view  the  present  manufacturing  technique.  A 
clause  on  sampling  and  inspection  has  been  added.  I  he  test  methods  have  been  brought  in  line  with 
the  test  methods  covered  in  other  similar  standards  of  eye  surgery  instruments.
